attribution.note: Zitron's own firm denial in his newsletter, with his own 'at scale' and salaried-positions clarifications.

semantics.note: Unhedged 'No it's not' with author's 'at scale' qualifier preserved. Omits 'salaried positions' scope, a minor narrowing kept in contract.

contract.note: Plain reading (material AI substitution for junior coders, July 2025 snapshot) is ordinary and fair; requires causal, coder-specific evidence and notes absence of proof is not proof of absence.

evidence.note: Stanford preprint revision (available 2026-08, before eval date) reports 15% July 2025 shortfall for young workers in AI-exposed occupations, but broad occupations, acknowledged pre-trends, no causal count of junior coders replaced.

reviews.rationale: Firm observation scored on a fair plain reading. The only evidence is occupation-level, descriptive, with pre-trends, and does not isolate junior coders or AI substitution at scale. It neither establishes absence nor presence of large-scale replacement, so the packet does not settle the claim.

attribution.note: Zitron's own arithmetic and estimates in his newsletter.

semantics.note: Weekly 3.5% share is a firm observation; the sub-3% monthly part rests on MAU figures he flagged as 'likely' guesses, so that component is hedged and not scored.

contract.note: Paid-share reading and July-Aug 2025 window are reasonable; requires matched, consistently defined counts and overlap checks, which is fair. Monthly component depends on guessed denominator.

evidence.note: OpenAI disclosure, Aug 7 2025: ~700M weekly users and 5M business paid users; denominator only, company disclosure.
TechCrunch Aug 2025 reports 5M paying business users; confirms one numerator component, no overlap data.
Epoch AI (Dec 2025) states 35M consumer subscribers July 2025, implying a higher weekly share, but secondary, untraced to primary, no overlap reconciliation; insufficient to contradict on its own.

reviews.rationale: Monthly sub-3% component rests on self-declared guessed MAU and is not scored; no MAU count exists in packet (and 25M/800M is 3.125%, not below 3%). Weekly 3.5% share is challenged by a secondary 35M-subscriber figure, but without primary sourcing or overlap reconciliation the matched counts the contract requires are absent.
